The statement acknowledges a sharp negative real-economy shock from COVID-19 but pairs it with an unusually forceful monetary response—cutting the policy rate to the effective lower bound and launching large-scale purchases of Treasuries and MBS, expanded repos, a deeper discount-window cut, and global dollar swap lines. Credit-channel research indicates these measures can materially ease the external finance premium and support investment and working capital, especially for constrained firms (Bernanke–Gertler; Gertler & Gilchrist 1994; Oliner & Rudebusch 1996a), helping to blunt the amplification that the financial accelerator would otherwise impart. At the zero lower bound/liquidity-trap risk, theory supports deploying balance-sheet tools and forward-looking inflation targeting to keep expectations anchored (Svensson 1997a; Svensson & Woodford 1999), consistent with the statement’s emphasis on subdued inflation pressures and stable survey expectations. The discount-window, reserve, and capital/liquidity-buffer actions directly target bank loan-supply constraints linked to capital and reserve requirements (Walsh & Wilcox; bank-capital literature), while dollar swap lines mitigate global funding stress. Netting these literature-backed mitigants against the near-term growth hit and elevated uncertainty shifts the tone from strongly negative to moderately negative.
